subject: Numeracy
title: Counting to 10
objectives: Children will say the number names from 1 to 10 in order.
Children will count steps, claps and jumps to 10.
content: Saying numbers to 10, number rhymes to 10, and counting steps and claps.
teachingActivities: Use rhythm and movement for number names 6 to 10; make a number line on the floor; count actions as well as objects; say numbers slowly and clearly; practise both forwards and, when ready, backwards.
learnerActivities: Say the number names from 1 to 10 in order and count actions to 10.
assessment: Observe whether each child says numbers to 10 in order and counts actions to 10.

lessons.title: Saying numbers to ten
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say the number names from one to ten in order.
successCriteria: Points to numerals as they say them
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to 5 objects and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
resources: A floor number line from 1 to 10
lessons.starter: Walk along a number line on the floor and say "Let us walk the numbers: one, two, three."
teacherActivities: Walk along the number line saying each number.
Point to each numeral and say it slowly.
Stop at a number and ask "What comes next?"
Walk the line again and count to ten.
learnerActivities: Children walk and say the numbers.
Children walk and count to ten.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk along the number line saying each number. Children: Children walk and say the numbers.
Step 2. Teacher: Point to each numeral and say it slowly. Children: Children repeat each number.
Step 3. Teacher: Stop at a number and ask "What comes next?" Children: Child says the next number.
Step 4. Teacher: Walk the line again and count to ten. Children: Children walk and count to ten.

practical.title: Walk the line
steps: Walk to ten saying each number.
Stop and say what comes next.
practical.safety: Keep the number line flat and secured so children do not trip. Walk slowly and one at a time.

differentiation.support: Walk the line holding the child’s hand and say the numbers softly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to walk backwards from ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says numbers to ten in order
lessons.conclusion: Count to ten together and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Count stairs or steps up to ten with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say the number names from one to ten in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Number rhymes to ten
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will sing and act number rhymes that count to ten.
successCriteria: Sings a rhyme with number actions
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to 5 objects and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
resources: A rhyme chart: ten little fingers
lessons.starter: Sing "Ten little fingers" and show ten fingers.
teacherActivities: Teach the rhyme line by line with finger actions.
Sing again and count the fingers from one to ten.
Add a drum beat for each number.
Let children act the rhyme in a circle.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Teach the rhyme line by line with finger actions. Children: Children copy the actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing again and count the fingers from one to ten. Children: Children count their fingers.
Step 3. Teacher: Add a drum beat for each number. Children: Children clap with each beat.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children act the rhyme in a circle. Children: Children act and count.

practical.title: Ten fingers rhyme
practical.safety: Keep the movement seated and gentle. Make sure the drum is not too loud for sensitive children.

differentiation.support: Sing slowly and count on fingers beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count ten fingers backwards.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Sing the rhyme once more and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing ten little fingers together at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing and act number rhymes that count to ten" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Ten little fingers, ten little toes.

lessons.title: Counting steps and claps
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count actions such as steps, claps and jumps to ten.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to 5 objects and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
lessons.starter: Clap your hands and say "Let us count my claps. One, two, three."
teacherActivities: Clap up to ten times slowly and ask children to count.
Walk ten steps across the room counting aloud.
Ask "How many jumps did we do?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Clap up to ten times slowly and ask children to count. Children: Children count the claps.
Step 2. Teacher: Walk ten steps across the room counting aloud. Children: Children walk and count steps.
Step 3. Teacher: Jump ten times together. Children: Children jump and count.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many jumps did we do?" Children: Child says ten.

practical.title: Count the action
practical.safety: Clear the floor of hazards and leave space between children. Jump on a soft mat only.

differentiation.support: Count to five and then add on with the teacher.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose an action and count to ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Sit quietly and count slow breaths to five.
lessons.homeConnection: Count claps, hops or jumps with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count actions such as steps, claps and jumps to ten" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Number hop
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will hop or jump along numerals 1 to 10 saying each number.
successCriteria: Jumps from number to number in order
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to 5 objects and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
resources: Large numerals 1 to 10 on the floor
lessons.starter: Put large numerals on the floor and say "Today we hop along the numbers."
teacherActivities: Show how to jump from one to two to three.
Let children take turns to jump along the numerals.
Ring the bell and call a number.
learnerActivities: Child jumps and says each number.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to jump from one to two to three. Children: Children watch and copy.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children take turns to jump along the numerals. Children: Child jumps and says each number.
Step 3. Teacher: Ring the bell and call a number. Children: Child jumps to that number.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise each child for counting. Children: Children clap and cheer.

practical.title: Number hop
practical.safety: Use a soft non-slip mat and keep the numerals flat. Supervise each hop and let one child go at a time.

differentiation.support: Walk along the numbers holding hands.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to hop in twos.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Pick up the numerals and say them aloud.
lessons.homeConnection: Chalk numbers on the ground and hop along them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hop or jump along numerals 1 to 10 saying each number" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 2 counting to ten check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how far each child counts in order.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count up to 5 objects and recognise numerals 1 to 5.
lessons.starter: Sing the number rhyme and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: walk the line, clap count and numeral order.
At each station ask the child to count and watch.
Record each child’s level and highest number counted.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: walk the line, clap count and numeral order. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask the child to count and watch. Children: Child counts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and highest number counted. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Counting stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Keep the drum volume gentle.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and count to five.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to count to fifteen.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says numbers to 10 in order; counts actions; sings number rhymes; says what comes next.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep counting to ten in daily life.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how far each child counts in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
